text:
English construction: Imperative
Example: “Keep the receipt. Do not fold the map.”
The base verb issues an instruction; do not forms the negative instruction.

English construction: Yes–no question
Example: “Did you lock the shed?”
Auxiliary did precedes the subject, and lock remains in its base form.

text:
English construction: Subject question
Example: “Who locked the shed?”
Who is the subject; this ordinary affirmative question does not need do-support.

text:
English construction: Object question
Example: “Which shed did you lock?”
The questioned object moves to the front while did precedes the subject.

English construction: Embedded question
Example: “I wonder which shed you locked.”
The embedded clause uses subject–verb order rather than the order of a direct question.

English construction: Question tag
Example: “The gate is open, isn't it?”
A positive statement can take a negative tag when seeking confirmation.

English construction: Negative statement with positive tag
Example: “You haven't seen the key, have you?”
